KANAWANA IN THE CANADIAN ALMANAC, EDITION BY EDITION
"Post Offices and Railroad Stations in Canada"
Swept 2026-09-07 from the Internet Archive's canadianalmanacd* items.

=====================================================================
THE LEGEND, WHICH IS THE WHOLE INSTRUMENT
=====================================================================

Every edition prints it above the table. The 1951 wording:

  "The Offices printed in italics are authorized to issue and pay Money
  Orders ... The Offices marked * are Savings Bank Offices. [dagger] Places
  marked thus are NOT Post Offices. ... The population of all cities, towns,
  and organized villages is shown to the right of places ... A large number
  of post offices and railway points are not incorporated, consequently have
  no population figure shown."

The 1968 wording is the same in substance: "The Offices marked * are Savings
Bank Offices. Places marked [dagger] are not Post Offices."

SO THE DAGGER IS THE CLOSING SIGNAL. A name in this table without a dagger is
an operating post office; the same name with one is a place that is not.
Kanawana never carries a population figure, which the legend explains: it was
never an incorporated place.

THE DAGGER SURVIVES OCR AS t, f, !, [ OR J, depending on the scan. Read it
against its neighbours on the same page rather than against a character list:
Kananaskis and Kanasuta carry it in every edition below, and Kanata and
Kandahar never do, so the two of them calibrate each scan.

=====================================================================
THE RUNS, VERBATIM FROM THE OCR
=====================================================================

1910 edition (vol. 63, copyright 1909) -- KANAWANA ABSENT, RUN CLEAN:
  "Kamouraska | Kamsack | Kananaskis . . , | Kanata | Kanes | Kanyengeh |
   Kaposvar . . , | Kars"
  No gap, no garbling, and no Kanawana. THIS NULL IS CONTROLLED.

1911 edition (vol. 64, title page "FOR THE YEAR 1911", Sixty-Fourth Year of
Publication, copyright 1910) -- PRESENT:
  "Kanata ... | Kanawana | Kanes . . | Kanyengeh | Kaposvar"

1912 edition (vol. 65) -- NOT DETERMINED. The name column in that scan is
interleaved with the district and station columns ("Kanata | Strathcona |
Alta | Erskine 538-114 | Jocelyn | Bathurst Village ...") and cannot be read
as a run. THE ABSENCE OF THE STRING IS NOT EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE FROM THE PAGE.

1917 and 1918 editions -- present. (Read in an earlier session; running
headers "[1917" and "[1918" confirmed here, against a suspicion that the
copyright year and the edition year are offset. They are offset in the 1911
volume and not in the 1918 one, so THE RUNNING HEADER IS THE THING TO READ.)

1943 edition -- present, columns legible: "Kanawana ...... Terrebonne ......
Q | St. Sauveur 529 or Piedmont 535".

1951 edition (_h4a6) -- PRESENT, NO DAGGER:
  "'Kamsack. ..1,754 | tKananaskis. . | t Kanasuta . | Kanawana ."
  The volume states its own year three ways: title page "DIRECTORY FOR 1951",
  "Copyright, Canada, 1951", running head "[1951".

1954 edition (_o8e8) -- PRESENT, NO DAGGER:
  "' Kainsack. ..2,327 | t Kananaakis . | tKanasuta . | Kanawana ."
  Title page "DIRECTORY FOR 1954", "Copyright, Canada, 1954", head "[1954".

1956 edition (_c3n5) -- PRESENT, NO DAGGER, AND NEARLY MISSED:
  "*Kamsack. ..2,327 | t Kananaskis . | t Kanasuta . | Kanavvana . |
   Kandahar ... .76 | Kane . | Kapasiwin"
  THE OCR READS THE W AS TWO V'S. A plain search for "Kanawana" returns
  nothing in this edition and the Internet Archive's own search-inside
  returns nothing, which would have made 1956 the closing year on a false
  null. Found by anchoring on Kanasuta and reading the run.

1957 edition (_t1a1) -- PRESENT, DAGGERED:
  "* Kamloops 8,099 | [Kamloops Jet. | Kamauraska ,48s | ... | t Kananaskis .
   | t Kanasuta . | [Kanawana . | Kandahar _ 76 | Kane ."
  THE BRACKET IS THE DAGGER IN THIS SCAN: Kamloops Junction, a railway point
  and not a post office, carries the same bracket, and Kandahar and Kane
  carry nothing.

1958 edition (_e0u3) -- PRESENT, DAGGERED: "KananaskisJ. | Kanasutaf . |
  Kanawanaf . | Kandahar"
1960 edition (_z0r2) -- PRESENT, DAGGERED: "Kananaskist .... | Kanasutaf . |
  Kanawanat . | Kandahar | Kane ."
1961 edition (_c6h2) -- PRESENT, DAGGERED, COLUMNS LEGIBLE:
  "Kanawanat . Terrebonne... .Q St. Sauveur des Mts 529 or [Piedmont 535]"
1962 edition (_y4m2) -- PRESENT, DAGGERED, COLUMNS LEGIBLE:
  "Kanawanat . Terrebonne. .. .Q St. Sauveur des Mts 529 or Piedmont 535"
1964, 1965, 1966 editions -- the string is present once in each; the runs
  were not read out.
1968 edition (_c4y7) -- PRESENT, DAGGERED:
  "Kamsack* . . | Kananaskis! .... | Kanasuta! . | Kanata . | Kanawana! . |
   Kandahar . | Kane ."

=====================================================================
WHAT THIS SETTLES
=====================================================================

THE OFFICE CLOSED BETWEEN THE 1956 AND 1957 EDITIONS. Unmarked in 1951, 1954
and 1956; daggered in 1957 and in every edition checked after. Since an
almanac edition is compiled the year before it is dated, that puts the
closure in 1956, or in the months between the two compilations.

This replaces the bracket this project had, "between about 1955 and the
mid-1960s", which rested on the two 1950s almanacs being undated and on a
McGraw-Hill directory catalogued 1966 that lists Kanawana among closed and
renamed offices with mail redirected to St-Sauveur-des-Monts. The McGraw-Hill
entry is not contradicted; it is just eight or ten years later than the event.

AND THE NAME OUTLIVED THE OFFICE BY AT LEAST TWELVE YEARS. Kanawana is still
in the table in 1968, still with Terrebonne and St. Sauveur des Monts beside
it, marked only as a place that is not a post office.

=====================================================================
THE EDITIONS THAT EXIST ON THE INTERNET ARCHIVE, WITH THEIR YEARS
=====================================================================

The archive catalogues every one of these as 1848, the series start, so the
year has to be read out of each volume. It is on the title page, as
"DIRECTORY FOR 19xx", within the first 45,000 bytes of the _djvu.txt -- a
range request is enough, no full download needed.

  1908 _b6y1   1910 _c2u2   1911 _g7p6   1914 _b2c5   1915 _g1q8
  1917 _y6g6   1918 _x3a0   1919 (no suffix)   1921 _y8r9   1922 _s0o3
  1943 _y9h2   1951 _h4a6   1952 _v6y8   1953 _y4p8   1954 _o8e8
  1956 _c3n5   1957 _t1a1   1958 _e0u3   1960 _z0r2   1961 _c6h2
  1962 _y4m2   1964 _v2i9   1965 _s8s5   1966 _p3n4   1968 _c4y7
  1970 _x1u8   1974 _l5j5

  Year not recovered from the first 45 KB: _a0q1 _b1t0 _b5o6 _i2q2 _m9i5
  _r7z1 _y9z7 _z6v3. (_y9h2 is also blank on this test but is known from an
  earlier session's reading to be the 1943 edition, which is a reminder that
  a blank here means the probe failed, not that the volume is undated.)

  And the older University of Toronto scans, whose suffix is the VOLUME
  NUMBER AND NOT THE YEAR -- a trap worth knowing, since canadianalmanacd63
  is the volume for 1910 and canadianalmanacd64 the volume for 1911:
  ...d22 ...d46 ...d48 ...d52 ...d53 ...d55 ...d62 ...d63 (1910)
  ...d64 (1911) ...d65 (1912)
